findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either resolve (with an observed status/body or doc citation) or explicitly downgrade to a non-load-bearing note the assertion that `/rest/api/2/reindex/issue` is not an effective synchronous foreground reindex on DC 8.17, and add observability so the helper's no-op is distinguishable from an effective reindex.
evidence: Plan states the helper 'had NO effect (and no observability — it no-ops silently), likely because /rest/api/2/reindex/issue is not an effective synchronous foreground reindex on DC 8.17' — an unverified negative capability claim presented as root-cause reasoning.

The in-repo helper (`_dc_support.py` L304-308) POSTs to `/rest/api/2/reindex/issue?issueId=...` and per its docstring returns silently on any failure, so its ineffectiveness cannot be distinguished from a no-op — the plan itself notes 'no observability'.

Retrieved Atlassian/ScriptRunner docs show DC reindex is normally driven via `IssueIndexingService.reIndex(...)` in-process, not asserted as a synchronous REST foreground operation — but no retrieved source confirms the specific 8.17 REST-endpoint behavior the plan asserts.
findings.finding: The load-bearing negative capability assertion that `/rest/api/2/reindex/issue` is not an effective synchronous foreground reindex on DC 8.17 is only hedged ('likely'), not resolved with evidence.
findings.location: Corrected root cause, paragraph 2 ('the forced-reindex helper had NO effect ... likely because /rest/api/2/reindex/issue is not an effective synchronous foreground reindex on DC 8.17')

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the documented Atlassian read-after-write consistency contract (JQL search eventually-consistent vs. direct issue GET) as prior art backing candidate #1, confirming the fix is the established read-your-writes pattern rather than a novel mechanism.
evidence: developer.atlassian.com 'Search and Reconcile' / 'Search After Write' documents the eventual-consistency read-after-write pattern for JQL search; Atlassian community: 'Jira Cloud does not guarantee immediate read-after-write consistency for JQL searches ... search results may temporarily return stale data until the index is updated.'

The plan anchors the insight to internal prior art (ADR 0085 §3 'index lag is unbounded', the existing bound-but-absent direct-GET seam) but presents the JQL-vs-direct-GET asymmetry as its own discovery rather than documented remote behavior.
This is a well-trodden read-your-writes pattern, not a novel architecture — so the gap is a coaching nudge, not a novelty-justification failure.
findings.finding: The plan reframes the root cause as novel-ish without acknowledging the documented external prior art (Atlassian's own guidance that JQL search is NOT read-after-write consistent while direct issue reads are, and the 'Search and Reconcile' / 'Search After Write' reconcile pattern) that its direct-GET-confirmation fix mirrors.
findings.location: Corrected root cause; Candidate resolution 1 ('outbound differ confirms a snapshot-detected field change via a bounded direct GET')
